literal: Battle midst path will-cut-off untrained horse those-who-are-like than-friends solitude is-best.
translation: Solitude is far better than the friendship of those who are like an untrained horse that throws its rider in the midst of battle.
modern: போர்க்களத்தின் நடுவே கீழே தள்ளிவிட்டு ஓடும் பழக்கப்படாத குதிரையைப் போன்றவர்களின் நட்பை விட, ஒருவன் தனியாக இருப்பதே மிகவும் சிறந்தது.
explanation: This couplet compares unreliable friends to an untrained horse in battle. Just as a wild horse might panic and throw its rider right when the fighting is fiercest, a bad friend will abandon you in times of crisis. The word 'மா' generally means animal but here specifically refers to a horse used in war. Therefore, the text concludes that facing life's struggles completely alone is much safer and better than relying on such treacherous companions.
